title: Matrix codes on 26/27-cell rectangles (2x13, 13x2, 3x9, 9x3): any pair-for-pair substitution, two-square and four-square, pairing widths 1-48
k4_result: Part 1 (any one-to-one table of letter pairs, no key): 310 of 2,352 pairings (w = 1..48, every block start) are impossible; ordinary pairs (w = 1) survive at both starts, w = 7 at 1 of 14 starts, w = 21 at 2 of 42. Part 2 on the 465 survivors with 6+ full clue pairs. Two-square: 3,720 settings (pairing x output order x grid); only 18 can be satisfied by ANY two squares (0 on 2x13, 0 on 3x9, 7 on 13x2, 11 on 9x3, all at w = 41-45); ordinary pairs are impossible on all four grids, both starts, both orders. On those 18 the 666,993 alphabets (by rows or columns, ? first or last) gave 244,549 single-square survivors and 0 joined pairs of squares. Run on all 2,352 pairings, the any-squares test leaves nothing below w = 29 on 2x13, 13x2 and 3x9, and only w = 16 and 27 below 29 on 9x3. Four-square with plain squares A-Z or KRYPTOS by rows: 37,200 settings, 185 possible for some pair of cipher squares (none at w = 1), 4 single-square hits, 0 settings with both cipher squares. Nothing to read: 0 decryptions. Playfair on any rectangle is out because plain K stays K at letter 74.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s through the same code: Part 1 kills 301, 416, 232 pairings; two-square settings possible for some squares 25, 18, 21 (0 on 2x13 in all three); single-square survivors 168,479 / 177,103 / 33,642; joined 0, 0, 0. Four-square possible for some cipher squares 997, 1,098, 235; square hits 9, 2, 3; joined 0, 0, 0. K4 looks like the shuffled texts: no decryption on either side.
scope_limits: Two-square means: plain letter 1 is found in one square and letter 2 in the other, the cipher pair is the other two corners of their rectangle, in either order; both squares on the same grid; side by side or one above the other. The any-squares result is a necessary test (column and row capacities, no two letters in one cell) and is exact where it kills. Where it does not kill (18 settings at w = 41-45, and pairings with fewer than 6 full clue pairs, mostly w >= 29 where some clue letters have no partner) only the listed squares were tried: 666,993 alphabets in all (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms), written by rows or by columns, the ? first or last on 27 cells. Four-square: the plain squares must be A-Z or KRYPTOS written by rows (? first or last); other plain squares are covered only by Part 1. Pair ciphers with a changing square, with nulls, or after a transposition are not covered. Clue positions are taken as exact. 'tested' counts single-square checks (every listed square against every column list and cell list of the 465 pairings); lists that no square can fit are counted as decided.

negative.family: Two-square / four-square / Playfair on 26- or 27-cell rectangles
negative.hypothesis: K4 is a 'matrix code' on letter pairs whose squares are 2x13, 13x2, 3x9 or 9x3 rectangles (26 letters, or 26 letters and the carved ?), so that all 26 letters can appear and K can stay K.
negative.scope: Pairings: letter i with letter i + w in blocks of 2w, w = 1..48, every block start, counted from the first letter or from the ? (2,352 pairings). Part 1: any one-to-one pair table. Two-square (both output orders, side by side or one above the other) on 2x13, 13x2, 3x9, 9x3: an exact no-key test for any two squares on all pairings, then 666,993 alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms) by rows or columns with the ? first or last, on the 465 Part 1 survivors with 6+ full clue pairs, filtered per square and hash-joined. Four-square with plain squares A-Z or KRYPTOS by rows, same grids, pairings and cipher-square list. 24 clue letters exact.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: ordinary pairs (w = 1) cannot be a two-square on any of the four grids with ANY squares, and no pairing below w = 29 can (except 9x3 at w = 16 and 27); the listed squares give 0 joined two-square settings and 0 four-square settings on K4 (controls: 3 shuffled K4s, 0 and 0 each; planted 4/4 found and read back among all 666,993 alphabets). Part 1 alone kills 310 of 2,352 pairings for every pair cipher. Playfair on a rectangle is out because K stays K.

follow_ups: Four-square with unknown plain squares: at w = 1 each full clue pair says 'cipher letter 1 sits in the row of plain letter 1 and the column of plain letter 2'. With all four squares free this is a capacity problem like the two-square one (rows hold C letters, columns R); a no-key test of it would close four-square on these grids without any alphabet list. Cost: seconds.
